questions.q: Cyclohexanone is heated with SeO₂. The organic product is:
questions.explain: In the Riley oxidation SeO₂ converts the α-CH₂ next to C=O into a second C=O, giving a 1,2-dicarbonyl compound; red selenium separates out.

questions.q: Cyclohexene is oxidised with SeO₂. The product is:
questions.explain: SeO₂ puts an OH on the allylic carbon and leaves the C=C in the ring. Diols and cleavage products come from KMnO₄, which attacks the double bond itself.

questions.q: Acetaldehyde (as paraldehyde) is oxidised with SeO₂. What are the products?
questions.explain: The α-CH₃ next to the C=O is converted into a second C=O, giving the 1,2-dicarbonyl OHC–CHO, while Se(IV) is reduced to red elemental selenium. No carbon is added or removed.

questions.q: The allylic oxidation of an alkene by SeO₂ is explained by which sequence of steps?
options: Radical abstraction of the allylic H, then capture by Br
Syn addition across C=C to form a cyclic ester, then hydrolysis to a diol
Ene reaction, then a [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement, then hydrolysis
Protonation of the alkene, carbocation formation, then attack by water
questions.explain: The ene step shifts the double bond and gives an allylseleninic acid; the [2,3]-sigmatropic shift moves the C=C back and puts O on the allylic carbon; hydrolysis releases the allylic alcohol. The radical route describes NBS bromination and the cyclic-ester route describes cold KMnO₄.
